newsitem.title: USA: Post-debate poll shows Kerry-Weld race a dead heat.
newsitem.headline: Post-debate poll shows Kerry-Weld race a dead heat.

text.p: A poll conducted for a local television station after Monday night's tough debate between Republican Gov. William Weld and incumbent Democrat John Kerry showed the U.S. Senate race was still too close to call.

The Mason Dixon Political Media Research group conducted the telephone survey after the debate for Boston's WHDH-TV, asking those questioned who they would vote for if the election were held Monday night.

Of those surveyed, 44 percent said they would vote for Kerry, 40 percent said they would vote for Weld and 13 percent said they were still undecided. The poll had a 5.1 percentage point margin of error.
The poll also asked who won the debate, and those surveyed said 44 percent thought Kerry had won, 35 percent thought Weld was the victor and 24 percent said it was a draw or they were unsure who won.
